about.ex: The trip takes about an hour.

acknowledged.ex: He acknowledged that the plan had problems.

example.en: Many doctors advocate free GP visits for all.
example.zh: 許多醫生提倡人人免費看家庭醫師。

note.meaning: （動詞）公開主張、提倡某做法；（名詞）倡導者。
note.usage: 動詞後直接接名詞或 V-ing（advocate reform / advocate doing），不加 for 較正式；名詞常見 an advocate for/of。

noteEn.meaning: To publicly support an idea or plan.
noteEn.usage: Use 'advocate something' or 'advocate doing'; noun: 'an advocate for'.

noteEs.exampleTr: Muchos médicos defienden visitas gratuitas al médico de cabecera para todos.
noteEs.meaning: Defender o promover públicamente una idea.
noteEs.usage: Va con sustantivo o -ing: advocate reform; como sustantivo: an advocate for.

noteHi.exampleTr: कई डॉक्टर सभी के लिए मुफ़्त GP मुलाक़ात का समर्थन करते हैं।
noteHi.meaning: किसी नीति या विचार का सार्वजनिक समर्थन करना।
noteHi.usage: सीधे संज्ञा या -ing के साथ: advocate reform; संज्ञा रूप: an advocate for।

noteJa.exampleTr: 多くの医師が全員の無料受診を提唱している。
noteJa.meaning: ある考えや政策を公に主張・提唱すること。
noteJa.usage: 目的語を直接とる：advocate reform。名詞は an advocate for。

noteKo.exampleTr: 많은 의사들이 모두를 위한 무료 일반의 진료를 주장한다.
noteKo.meaning: 어떤 정책이나 생각을 공개적으로 지지하고 주장하다.
noteKo.usage: 목적어를 바로 씀: advocate reform; 명사로는 an advocate for.

anticipated.ex: Sales are anticipated to rise next year.

approximately.ex: The journey takes approximately two hours.

archbishop.en: a senior bishop who leads a large area
archbishop.ex: The archbishop spoke at the cathedral on Sunday.

around.ex: Around fifty people came to the meeting.

as.en: in the same way; in the role of

asked.ex: The teacher asked us to be quiet.

asking.ex: They are asking the council for help.

assembly.en: a large formal meeting of people
assembly.ex: The assembly voted on ten proposals.

at.es: a (at the same rate: al mismo ritmo)
at.hi: पर (at the same rate: उसी दर पर)
at.ja: 〜で（at the same rate：同じ割合で）
at.zh: 以（at the same rate：以相同速度）

attended.ex: Hundreds of parents attended the school concert.

backed.ex: The plan is backed by local businesses.

be.ex: Try to be on time tomorrow.

becoming.ex: The city is becoming more crowded every year.

been.ex: It has been a busy week.

bishops.ex: The bishops met to discuss parish life.

bringing.en: causing to reach a state (bring to a close: end)
bringing.ex: The final song is bringing the show to a close.
bringing.zh: 帶到（bring to a close：結束）

called.ex: He called for a change in the law.

came.en: came to: reached a total of

candid.ex: She gave a candid interview about her career.

cast.ex: Millions of people cast their votes on Friday.

cent.ex: Prices rose by five per cent.

church.ex: The church runs many schools in Ireland.

church's.ex: The church's view on this has changed.

clerical.ex: Clerical and lay members met in the hall.

close.ex: The festival came to a close on Sunday.

closely.ex: Doctors are watching the patient closely.

co.en: short for County, an area of Ireland

commitment.en: being willing to work hard for something
commitment.ex: Her commitment to the team is clear.

concluded.en: decided something after thinking about it
concluded.ex: The doctor concluded that he needed rest.

conference.en: a formal group or meeting (bishops' conference)
conference.ex: The teachers' conference starts on Monday.

consequently.ex: It rained heavily; consequently, the match was cancelled.

considered.ex: The road is considered safe now.

consultation.ex: After consultation, the plan was changed.

example.en: The plan changed after a public consultation.
example.zh: 經過公眾諮詢後，計畫有所修改。

note.usage: public consultation；in consultation with sb = 與…協商。

noteEn.meaning: asking people for their opinions before deciding.

noteEs.exampleTr: El plan cambió tras una consulta pública.
noteEs.usage: public consultation; in consultation with sb.

noteHi.exampleTr: सार्वजनिक परामर्श के बाद योजना बदली।
noteHi.usage: public consultation; in consultation with sb।

noteJa.exampleTr: 意見公募の後、計画は変更された。

noteKo.usage: public consultation; in consultation with 사람.

consultative.ex: The council set up a consultative group of residents.

contingent.ex: The deal is contingent on government funding.

contrast.en: a clear difference (by contrast: in comparison)
contrast.ex: By contrast, the north had a dry summer.

convene.ex: The committee will convene again in spring.

example.en: The UN convened an emergency meeting on the crisis.
example.zh: 聯合國就這場危機召開了緊急會議。

note.usage: 主詞通常是政府、主席等主辦者；被動 be convened by 很常見。

noteEn.meaning: to bring people together for a formal meeting.
noteEn.usage: Used with 'meeting', 'summit', 'panel'; often passive: 'be convened by'.

noteEs.exampleTr: La ONU convocó una reunión de emergencia sobre la crisis.
noteEs.meaning: convocar una reunión o un evento.
noteEs.usage: Suele tener como sujeto un gobierno o presidente; la pasiva be convened by es frecuente.

noteHi.exampleTr: संयुक्त राष्ट्र ने संकट पर एक आपात बैठक बुलाई।
noteHi.usage: आमतौर पर सरकार या अध्यक्ष बुलाते हैं; be convened by भी आम है।

noteJa.exampleTr: 国連はその危機について緊急会合を招集した。
noteJa.meaning: 会議などを招集・開催する。
noteJa.usage: 主語は政府や議長が多く、受動態 be convened by もよく使う。

noteKo.exampleTr: 유엔은 그 위기에 관한 긴급 회의를 소집했다.
noteKo.usage: 주어는 주로 정부나 의장이며 수동태 be convened by도 흔하다.

convened.en: brought people together for a meeting
convened.ex: The mayor convened an urgent meeting on flooding.
convened.ja: 招集された；開催された

example.en: The UN convened an emergency meeting on the crisis.
example.zh: 聯合國就這場危機召開了緊急會議。

note.usage: 主詞通常是政府、主席等主辦者；被動 be convened by 很常見。

noteEn.meaning: to bring people together for a formal meeting.
noteEn.usage: Used with 'meeting', 'summit', 'panel'; often passive: 'be convened by'.

noteEs.exampleTr: La ONU convocó una reunión de emergencia sobre la crisis.
noteEs.meaning: convocar una reunión o un evento.
noteEs.usage: Suele tener como sujeto un gobierno o presidente; la pasiva be convened by es frecuente.

noteHi.exampleTr: संयुक्त राष्ट्र ने संकट पर एक आपात बैठक बुलाई।
noteHi.usage: आमतौर पर सरकार या अध्यक्ष बुलाते हैं; be convened by भी आम है।

noteJa.exampleTr: 国連はその危機について緊急会合を招集した。
noteJa.meaning: 会議などを招集・開催する。
noteJa.usage: 主語は政府や議長が多く、受動態 be convened by もよく使う。

noteKo.exampleTr: 유엔은 그 위기에 관한 긴급 회의를 소집했다.
noteKo.usage: 주어는 주로 정부나 의장이며 수동태 be convened by도 흔하다.

conversely.ex: Some like the plan; conversely, others hate it.

example.en: Cheap loans boost spending; conversely, high rates slow it.
example.zh: 低息貸款刺激消費；相反地，高利率會抑制消費。

note.usage: 常置句首加逗號，用來引出與前句相反的情況。

noteEn.usage: Often starts a sentence with a comma to give the opposite case.

noteEs.exampleTr: Los préstamos baratos impulsan el gasto; por el contrario, los tipos altos lo frenan.
noteEs.meaning: De forma opuesta; por el contrario.
noteEs.usage: Suele ir al inicio con coma para presentar la situación opuesta.

noteHi.exampleTr: सस्ते ऋण खर्च बढ़ाते हैं; इसके विपरीत, ऊँची दरें उसे धीमा करती हैं।
noteHi.usage: प्रायः वाक्य के आरंभ में अल्पविराम के साथ, उल्टी स्थिति बताने के लिए।

noteJa.exampleTr: 低金利の融資は消費を促し、逆に高金利は消費を抑える。
noteJa.usage: 文頭でカンマとともに使い、前文と逆の状況を示す。

noteKo.exampleTr: 저금리 대출은 소비를 늘리고, 반대로 고금리는 소비를 줄인다.
noteKo.usage: 보통 문장 앞에 쉼표와 함께 써서 반대 상황을 제시.

create.ex: The factory will create 200 new jobs.

current.ex: The current rules are too strict.

deacon.en: a church role below a priest
deacon.ex: The deacon read from the Bible at Mass.

deacons.en: people with a church role below priests
deacons.ex: Two new deacons joined the parish this year.

debate.en: a discussion where people give opinions
debate.ex: There was a long debate about school fees.

deemed.ex: The bridge was deemed unsafe after the flood.

defeated.ex: The plan was defeated in a close vote.

delegates.en: people sent to a meeting to represent others
delegates.ex: Delegates from forty countries attended the talks.

example.en: Delegates from 40 countries attended the summit.
example.zh: 來自40國的代表出席了峰會。

note.usage: delegates to/at a conference；動詞 delegate = 委派。

noteEn.meaning: people sent to a meeting to represent others.

noteEs.exampleTr: Delegados de 40 países asistieron a la cumbre.
noteEs.usage: delegates at a conference; verbo delegate = delegar.

noteHi.exampleTr: 40 देशों के प्रतिनिधि शिखर सम्मेलन में आए।
noteHi.usage: delegates at a conference; क्रिया delegate = सौंपना।

noteJa.exampleTr: 40か国の代表がサミットに出席した。
noteJa.usage: delegates at a conference；動詞 delegate は「任せる」。

noteKo.usage: delegates at a conference; 동사 delegate는 '위임하다'.

deliberations.ex: The jury began its deliberations on Monday.

example.en: After two days of deliberations, the panel reached a decision.
example.zh: 經過兩天審議，小組作出了決定。

note.usage: 多用複數；jury/committee deliberations；after much deliberation。

noteEs.exampleTr: Tras dos días de deliberaciones, el comité decidió.

noteHi.exampleTr: दो दिन के विचार-विमर्श के बाद पैनल ने फ़ैसला किया।

noteJa.exampleTr: 2日間の審議の末、委員会は結論を出した。

noteKo.exampleTr: 이틀간의 심의 끝에 위원회가 결정을 내렸다.

destined.en: meant to go to a place or person
destined.ex: These boxes are destined for the new school.

develop.en: to make something grow or improve

devise.ex: We need to devise a better plan.

diaconate.en: the church role or rank of deacon
diaconate.ex: He was ordained to the diaconate last year.

diocesan.en: of a diocese (area led by a bishop)
diocesan.ex: The diocesan office handles school funding.

dioceses.en: church areas each led by a bishop

direction.ex: The company is moving in a new direction.

discernment.en: careful judgement, often in religious decisions
discernment.ex: The decision needs time and discernment.

example.en: Choosing the right path requires careful discernment.
example.zh: 選擇正確的道路需要審慎的辨別。

note.meaning: （審慎的）辨明；判斷力；宗教語境指「分辨上主旨意」。
note.usage: need/require discernment；正式、偏宗教或文學用語。

noteEn.meaning: careful judgement about what is right.

noteEs.exampleTr: Elegir el camino correcto requiere un discernimiento cuidadoso.
noteEs.usage: require discernment; frecuente en contexto religioso.

noteHi.exampleTr: सही रास्ता चुनने के लिए सावधान विवेक चाहिए।
noteHi.usage: require discernment; धार्मिक संदर्भ में आम।

noteJa.exampleTr: 正しい道を選ぶには慎重な見極めが必要だ。
noteJa.usage: require discernment；宗教的文脈でよく使う。

noteKo.exampleTr: 올바른 길을 고르려면 신중한 식별이 필요하다.
noteKo.usage: require discernment; 종교적 맥락에서 자주 쓴다.

discussion.ex: We had a long discussion about the plan.

dissented.ex: Two judges dissented from the ruling.

down.ex: The plan was voted down by the board.

due.ex: The train is due at six.

encompassing.ex: The park is huge, encompassing three lakes.

end.ex: We left at the end of the film.

endorsed.ex: The minister endorsed the new plan.

entire.ex: The entire village came to the festival.

envisaged.en: planned or imagined as part of the future
envisaged.ex: The architect envisaged a garden on the roof.

establish.en: to create or set up something lasting

example.en: The city plans to establish a new art centre.
example.zh: 市政府計畫設立一個新的藝術中心。

note.usage: establish a company/office/system；也指「證實」establish the facts。

noteEn.meaning: to create or set up something that lasts.

noteEs.exampleTr: La ciudad quiere crear un nuevo centro de arte.
noteEs.usage: establish a company/office; establish the facts = comprobar.

noteHi.exampleTr: शहर एक नया कला केंद्र स्थापित करना चाहता है।
noteHi.usage: establish a company/office; establish the facts = तथ्य साबित करना।

noteJa.exampleTr: 市は新しいアートセンターの設立を計画している。
noteJa.usage: establish an office/system；establish the facts は「事実を立証する」。

noteKo.exampleTr: 시는 새 예술 센터 설립을 계획하고 있다.
noteKo.usage: establish an office/system; establish the facts는 '사실을 밝히다'.

even.en: used for surprise (even though: despite the fact)
even.ex: She came even though she was ill.

examination.ex: A closer examination showed new problems.

felt.ex: Many felt the plan was unfair.

find.en: to discover; to feel that (find it hard)
find.ex: Many people find it hard to save money.
find.zh: 發現；感到（find it hard：覺得困難）

first.ex: It was her first trip to Ireland.

five-year.ex: The government announced a five-year plan.

form.en: the way something exists or is organised
form.ex: The plan will change its form over time.

forwarded.ex: I forwarded your email to the manager.

future.ex: Future students will benefit from the change.

garnered.ex: The idea garnered support from many teachers.

gathered.ex: Friends gathered in the park for a picnic.

go.en: to move; to be given (go up: rise)
go.ja: 行く；上がる・下がる（go up/down）

grounded.ex: Her advice is grounded in long experience.

had.ex: She had a small shop in the town.

held.ex: The school held a concert in May.

however.ex: It was sunny; however, it was cold.

ideas.ex: Send us your ideas for the party.

inaugural.en: first in a series of events
inaugural.ex: The inaugural race was held in 1990.

example.en: The inaugural festival attracted ten thousand visitors.
example.zh: 首屆音樂節吸引了一萬名遊客。

note.meaning: 首屆的、第一次舉辦的；本文指第一屆食物分享高峰會。
note.usage: 只放在名詞前，常搭配 event、summit、season 等；也可指就職的（inaugural speech）。

noteEn.meaning: first in a series of events.
noteEn.usage: Use it only before a noun, e.g. inaugural summit.

noteEs.exampleTr: El festival inaugural atrajo a diez mil visitantes.
noteEs.meaning: primero de una serie de eventos.
noteEs.usage: Va delante del sustantivo (inaugural summit); también significa de investidura.

noteHi.exampleTr: पहले उत्सव में दस हज़ार लोग आए।
noteHi.usage: केवल संज्ञा से पहले आता है, जैसे inaugural summit; उद्घाटन भाषण के लिए भी।

noteJa.exampleTr: 第1回のフェスティバルには1万人が訪れた。
noteJa.meaning: 第1回の；初めて開かれる。
noteJa.usage: 名詞の前だけで使う（inaugural summit）。就任の意味もある。

noteKo.exampleTr: 첫 번째 축제에는 만 명이 방문했다.
noteKo.usage: 명사 앞에서만 쓴다(inaugural summit). 취임의 뜻도 있다.

inclusion.en: the act of including someone or something
inclusion.ex: The inclusion of children's books made the library popular.
inclusion.ja: 対象に含めること；包含

informed.ex: The teacher informed us about the test.

intended.ex: The money is intended for repairs.

kind.ex: What kind of music do you like?

language.en: a system of words used by a people
language.ex: Spanish is a popular language to learn.

lasted.ex: My old phone lasted for six years.

lasting.en: continuing for a length of time
lasting.ex: It was a meeting lasting three hours.

lay.ex: Lay members now run many church groups.

level.en: an amount or height on a scale
level.ex: The level of debt is too high.

many.ex: Many people work from home now.

marking.ex: The shop is marking its first year with a sale.

may.ex: Kids may start school at four.
may.ja: …かもしれない；…することがある

meet.en: to come together for a discussion
meet.ex: The bishops will meet in Maynooth.

meeting.en: an event where people gather to talk

members.en: people who belong to a group
members.ex: All members can vote at the meeting.

met.ex: We met at the café after work.

ministry.ex: He spent forty years in ministry.

most.ex: This is the most popular dish here.

national.ex: The national team won the match.

necessary.ex: Is it necessary to book a table?

needed.ex: More teachers are needed in rural areas.

nevertheless.ex: It was raining; nevertheless, we went out.

example.en: The test was hard; nevertheless, most students passed.
example.zh: 考試很難；儘管如此，大多數學生仍通過了。

note.usage: 承接前句轉折，常置句首加逗號或用分號連接；比 however 更強調「仍然」。

noteEn.usage: Often starts a sentence or follows a semicolon.

noteEs.exampleTr: El examen fue difícil; no obstante, la mayoría aprobó.
noteEs.usage: Al inicio de la frase o tras punto y coma.

noteHi.exampleTr: परीक्षा कठिन थी; फिर भी ज़्यादातर छात्र पास हुए।
noteHi.usage: वाक्य की शुरुआत में या semicolon के बाद।

noteJa.exampleTr: 試験は難しかったが、それでも大半が合格した。
noteJa.usage: 文頭やセミコロンの後に置く。

now.ex: The shop is now open on Sundays.

number.ex: The number of tourists is rising.

open.ex: We had an open talk about money.

openly.ex: They talked openly about their worries.

opposed.ex: Many locals are opposed to the new road.

ordinary.ex: It looks like an ordinary house.

ordination.en: making someone a priest or deacon
ordination.ex: His ordination took place in the cathedral.

outcome.ex: We are waiting for the outcome of the vote.

parish.ex: The parish hall hosts a weekly market.

parishes.ex: Several parishes now share one priest.

part.ex: Teachers will take part in the strike.

per.ex: The ticket costs ten euro per person.

present.ex: In its present form, the plan is too costly.

priest.en: a person who leads church services
priest.ex: The priest spoke to the families after Mass.

priests.ex: Two priests work at the cathedral.

primate.en: the most senior bishop of a country
primate.ex: The Primate led the national service.

process.en: a series of changes over time
process.ex: Learning a language is a slow process.

proposals.ex: The council will discuss the proposals next week.

quarter.ex: A quarter of the crop was lost.

recommendations.en: suggestions about what should be done

reflect.ex: Take time to reflect on your choice.

request.ex: The council agreed to our request.

required.en: made to do by a rule
required.ex: Students are required to wear uniforms.
required.ja: 義務づけられた（be required to）

respectful.ex: Please be respectful to other users.

respond.ex: How will the minister respond to the report?

results.en: things that happen because of an action
results.ex: The new diet gave good results.

role.ex: He has a key role in the team.

roles.ex: The company is hiring for several new roles.

sent.ex: I sent the form to the office yesterday.

significant.ex: There was a significant rise in rents.

some.ex: Some fifty people came to the meeting.

stated.ex: The report stated the facts clearly.

stock.en: take stock: think carefully about a situation
stock.ex: After the election, the party will take stock.

support.ex: The company will no longer support the old software.

supported.ex: The idea was supported by most voters.

survive.ex: Small shops struggle to survive online competition.

synodal.en: of a church meeting that listens to members

take.en: to do or have (take part, take stock)
take.ex: Many students take part in the club.
take.zh: 採取（take part：參加；take stock：檢討）

talks.ex: The two sides held talks yesterday.

terminology.en: special words used for a subject
terminology.ex: Medical terminology can be hard to learn.

theologically.en: in a way based on the study of religion

these.en: the ones here or just mentioned

think.ex: Let me think about your offer.

token.en: a sign or symbol of something
token.ex: He gave her flowers as a token of thanks.

took.en: took part: joined in; took to the streets: protested
took.ex: Many students took part in the race.
took.zh: took part：參加；took to the streets：上街

total.ex: The total cost was two million.

trouble.ex: The company is in trouble after losing its biggest client.

universal.ex: The universal church includes Catholics everywhere.

example.en: The current rate of spending is unsustainable.
example.zh: 目前的支出速度無法持續。

note.usage: unsustainable level/growth/debt；常說 in current form 下無法維持。

noteEn.meaning: not able to continue at the same level.

noteEs.exampleTr: El ritmo actual de gasto es insostenible.

noteHi.exampleTr: खर्च की मौजूदा दर टिकाऊ नहीं है।
noteHi.meaning: टिकाऊ नहीं; लंबे समय तक नहीं चल सकता।

noteJa.exampleTr: 現在の支出ペースは持続不可能だ。

untenable.ex: His position as captain became untenable.
untenable.hi: अस्वीकार्य; जिसे सही न ठहराया जा सके
untenable.ja: 擁護できない；維持できない

example.en: After the scandal, his position became untenable.
example.zh: 醜聞發生後，他的職位已無法保住。

note.meaning: （立場、看法或情況）站不住腳的、無法維持或辯護的。
note.usage: 多作表語，常見 position/situation becomes untenable；語氣正式。

paragraphs: About 300 Catholics met in Gormanston, Co Meath, on Saturday. It was the first meeting of its kind in Ireland. Both priests and ordinary church members came.
They voted on 35 ideas. These ideas will go to the bishops.

One idea was about women in the church. It asked for more open talks about women becoming deacons. A deacon is a church role below a priest. More than half of the people voted for it. About a quarter voted against it.
Another idea was a national office for women. Most people voted against this.
Archbishop Eamon Martin said many parishes are in trouble. The bishops will meet next week to talk about the results.

About 300 people met in Gormanston, Co Meath, on Saturday for the first National Synodal Assembly of Catholics in Ireland. Both priests and ordinary church members took part. The meeting ended a process that lasted five years.

The delegates voted on 35 proposals, which will now go to the bishops as recommendations. One proposal asked the church to talk openly and seriously about women's roles, including women becoming deacons. In total, 54 per cent supported it, 19 per cent said it needed more thought, and 27 per cent were against it.
A plan for a national office for women was rejected, with 56 per cent voting against. A majority supported asking the wider church to develop respectful language for LGBT+ people.
Archbishop Eamon Martin said many parishes, and even some dioceses, will find it hard to survive in their current form. He said the bishops would meet next week to think about the results.

Around 300 lay and clerical delegates gathered in Gormanston, Co Meath, on Saturday for the first National Synodal Assembly of Catholics in Ireland, marking the end of a five-year consultation process.

Delegates voted on 35 proposals, which will be sent to the bishops as recommendations. The most closely watched called for open, serious and theologically informed discussion of women's ministry, including ordination to the diaconate. It was backed by 54 per cent of delegates, while 19 per cent felt it needed further discernment and 27 per cent were opposed.

However, a proposal to create a national office for women, intended to show the church's commitment to including women at parish and diocesan level, was defeated, with 56 per cent voting against. A majority supported asking the universal church to develop respectful vocabulary for LGBT+ people.

Archbishop Eamon Martin, the Catholic Primate, said the process was necessary because many parishes and even dioceses are unsustainable in their current form. The bishops' conference will meet next week to reflect on the outcome.

Some 300 lay and clerical delegates convened in Gormanston, Co Meath, on Saturday for the inaugural National Synodal Assembly of Catholics in Ireland, bringing a five-year consultative process to a close.

Delegates cast votes on 35 proposals destined for the bishops as recommendations. The most keenly anticipated urged a candid, theologically grounded debate on women's ministry, encompassing ordination to the diaconate. It garnered the support of 54 per cent, while 19 per cent deemed it in need of further discernment and 27 per cent dissented.

By contrast, a proposed national office for women, envisaged as a token of the church's commitment to their full inclusion in parishes and dioceses, was voted down by 56 per cent. A majority endorsed asking the universal church to devise respectful vocabulary for LGBT+ people.

Archbishop Eamon Martin, the Catholic Primate, acknowledged that numerous parishes, and even entire dioceses, are untenable in their present form. The bishops' conference is due to convene next week to take stock of the deliberations.

Approximately 300 lay and clerical delegates attended the first National Synodal Assembly of Catholics in Ireland, held in Gormanston, Co Meath, on Saturday, which concluded a consultation process lasting five years.

Participants voted on 35 proposals that will be forwarded to the bishops as formal recommendations. The most significant proposal advocated a serious and theologically informed examination of the role of women in ministry, including ordination to the diaconate. It received the support of 54 per cent of delegates; nevertheless, 19 per cent considered that further discernment was required, and 27 per cent were opposed.

Conversely, a proposal to establish a national office for women was rejected by 56 per cent of participants. A majority, however, supported a request that the universal church develop respectful terminology for LGBT+ people.

Archbishop Eamon Martin, the Catholic Primate, stated that the process had been essential, since a substantial number of parishes and dioceses are unsustainable in their current form. Consequently, the future direction of the church in Ireland may be contingent upon how the bishops respond when they meet next week.
